detail.title: Nonreciprocal Coupling and Coarse-Grained Dissipation Bounds
detail.summary: Thermodynamic dissipation in nonequilibrium systems is intrinsically constrained by the resolution of the information-processing mechanism. While generalized TURs provide lower bounds on entropy production, finite-information reconstruction—specifically propagation delay and observer-relative bandwidth—further refines the effective dissipation cost. True predictive memory requires operational sufficiency, where state persistence is insufficient without corresponding reductions in future uncertainty.
detail.reason: Revising the project notebook to incorporate new operational constraints on information flow and finite-information reconstruction which challenge previous assumptions of infinite-resolution feedback.

detail.title: Predictive Information and Dissipation Bounds
detail.question: What is the theoretical relationship between predictive information and thermodynamic dissipation in nonequilibrium systems with finite or noisy memory?
detail.reason: Continuing the active project within the enforced predictive_dissipation topic.

detail.title: Predictive Dissipation and Information Bounds Synthesis
detail.summary: This cycle advances the investigation into the thermodynamic cost of predictive memory by synthesizing coarse-graining limits with thermodynamic uncertainty relations. The existing notebook on dissipation bounds has been revised to integrate findings on finite-information reconstruction and the operational definitions of information flow, establishing a framework that bridges stochastic thermodynamics with information-theoretic limits.
